subject: Context strategy & model-choice checklist for KiteTek onboarding
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
To: Alyssa Moore <alyssa@kitetek.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:15:23-07:00
Subject: Context strategy & model-choice checklist for KiteTek onboarding

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, attaching a short checklist to align on context needs and a pragmatic model shortlist so the implementation team can start sizing. High level asks from our side before the implementation kickoff:

1) Confirm representative prompt + response samples (attached: kitetek_context_sample.json).
2) Expected peak concurrent sessions during initial 90 days and monthly active users (MAU) estimate.
3) Any regulatory constraints around context retention (e.g., must not persist PII beyond X hours).

Quick summary we discussed:
- Primary use: conversational assistant inside product (ticket triage + feature guidance).
- Typical turn length: 1–2 user messages then a system / assistant reply.
- Target latency: p95 generation <= 450ms for short responses, <= 1.2s for long-form.

Model shortlist (first-pass — performance vs cost tradeoffs):
- rwdx-7b-quant (low-cost, good for short context workflows, 8k context OK)
- openchat-8b (balanced; better instruction quality, 16k context available)
- rwdx-14b-int8 (higher quality for multi-step reasoning, 32k context recommended)

See attached KiteTek_MA_plan.xlsx for the session and traffic assumptions you gave on the call.

Next step: Monica will share token-volume estimates per model variant and a quick throughput recommendation so you can lock the kickoff date. Can we target Oct 20 for a 60-minute tech handoff?

Thanks,

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks, Sean — this is great.

Couple of clarifying items:
- MAU: initial rollout ~8k MAU, expected to ramp to 45k over 6 months. Peak concurrent sessions estimate is rough: 420 concurrent during product peak.
- Typical prompt/response: user prompts average 180 tokens, assistant replies average 320 tokens in production.
- We have a legal requirement to expire chat context after 30 days; no permanent storage of raw PII.

We can confirm Oct 20 for the tech handoff. Please send the token-volume estimates — that's what procurement will use for early budget planning.

Also: can you confirm whether the 16k/32k context modes for the larger models will be billed differently or only by token usage? 

Best,
Alyssa

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
To: Alyssa Moore <alyssa@kitetek.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-12T14:38:12-07:00
Subject: Re: Context strategy & model-choice checklist for KiteTek onboarding

Hi Alyssa,

Thanks for the MAU numbers — those help a lot. Below are conservative token-volume and throughput estimates for each candidate model given your session profile. I included both per-session and monthly projections so procurement has a ballpark.

Assumptions:
- Initial MAU: 8,000; steady-state month 6 MAU: 45,000 (we'll show both sets)
- Avg user prompt: 180 tokens; Avg assistant reply: 320 tokens => Avg roundtrip: 500 tokens
- Peak concurrency (initial): 420
- Peak concurrency (ramp): 2,400

Model estimates (initial ramp / month 1 — ramp month 6):

1) rwdx-7b-quant (8k context)
- Per-session tokens (avg): 500
- Monthly tokens (initial MAU): 8,000 * 500 * 12 sessions/mo ~ 48,000,000 tokens
- Monthly tokens (month 6 MAU): 45,000 * 500 * 12 ~ 270,000,000 tokens
- Throughput notes: good for high-concurrency low-latency use; recommend 6–8 concurrent streams per GPU (depends on instance type). Expected p95 gen 200–500ms for short replies.

2) openchat-8b (16k context)
- Per-session tokens: 500 (but larger answers possible; provision for 700 tokens in heavy flows)
- Monthly tokens (initial): ~56,000,000 (using 700 tokens for heavy flows estimate)
- Monthly tokens (month 6): ~378,000,000
- Throughput: moderate; 4–6 streams per GPU. Good tradeoff of quality vs cost.

3) rwdx-14b-int8 (32k context)
- Per-session tokens: 500–900 (depends on long-context dialogue); use 700 tokens avg conservative
- Monthly tokens (initial): ~67,200,000
- Monthly tokens (month 6): ~378,000,000
- Throughput: 2–3 streams per GPU for low latency; best choice if you need 32k context for multi-turn diagnostics/retention.

Pricing note: Redwood bills by tokens for hosted usage; context-window availability (16k vs 32k) does not change billing unit price but larger models tend to have higher per-token cost due to compute. We'll include model-specific cost estimates in the formal SOW.

Operational recommendations:
- Start with rwdx-7b-quant for the initial rollout to control cost and validate flows.
- Keep openchat-8b as a higher-quality fallback for ticket escalation routes.
- Reserve a canary pool of rwdx-14b-int8 for any flows that need long-context retrieval (e.g., multi-ticket threads).

I'll attach a short sizing sheet for the infra and suggested initial reserved GPU counts based on your projected peak concurrency (see KiteTek_MA_plan.xlsx).

Let me know if you want these broken out by region (we can split US/EU if you expect EU users during early months).

Thanks,

Monica Patel
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.inference
